editorial.description_en: The bottom of a pool that has one. Dark blue-green, and the last point at which the hue is still readable.
editorial.description_ja: 深い淵の底のような、暗い青緑。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.296, C 0.042, h 186.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 深 (shin, deep) + 淵 (en, pool). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Deep Pool" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 深淵. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — iwa-hada at ΔE00 7.8, fuyu-sugi at ΔE00 8.8, tetsu-midori at ΔE00 9.0. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (6°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
